newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Cetes rates fall again on stable peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Cetes rates fall again on stable peso.

text.p: Mexico's Cetes rates continued their downard slide on Tuesday at Banco de Mexico's primary auction as the peso remained stable on strong capital inflows, analysts said.
The rate on the bellwether one-month paper fell a sharp 126 basis points to 22.98 percent, after falling 147 basis points the week before.
A Reuters' survey of 10 Cetes dealers found expectations of a more modest 49 basis points decline on the 28-day paper this week.
Demand was 13.8 billion pesos this week compared with 3.3 billion pesos worth on offer. Demand was much stronger than the 9.63 billion pesos last week.
"Foreign funds are continuing to enter into the country and the expectations for inflation for February are favourable," said Banco Union analyst Ricardo Vazquez.

The decline in primary interest rates came even though the central bank drained liquidity from the secondary money market on Tuesday, which could have been an attempt to put a floor under falling rates, analysts said.
In late December, the rate on the key one-month paper was 27.39 percent, but it has fallen steadily since on strong capital inflows and declining inflation expectations.
"Interest rates also display the influence of incoming capital: since the start of the year, rates have fallen at all maturities...," J.P. Morgan wrote in a recent report.
Market analysis company MMS International said that dollar repatriation from Mexican subsidiaries abroad and high liquidity levels contributed to the strong peso and lower Cetes rates.
Mexico's bolsa is also showing signs of the strong capital inflows, rising to a record close on Tuesday.
The stock market had its sixth record close in seven trading sessions, which traders said was mainly fuelled by a bullish Dow Jones and forecasts of further falls in domestic interest rates.
Expectations of lower inflation are allowing interest rates to drop and for the yield curve to flatten out, analysts said.

"The short-term portion of the curve has flattened dramatically since late December, arguably a direct indication that the market's inflation outlook has become more positive," J.P. Morgan said in its market report.
This week the rate on the three-month paper fell 50 basis points to 24.43 percent, while the six month paper rate showed a decline of 84 basis points to 24.68 percent.
The yield on one-year paper was 25.54 percent this week compared with 26.0 percent last week.
Expectations that the peso could weaken during the year may have moderated declines in the longer-term paper, analysts said.
